name: KAGRA — dark matter searches
full_name: Kamioka Gravitational Wave Detector dark-matter searches
summary: A Japanese underground cryogenic gravitational-wave detector conducting an independent ultralight vector-dark-matter search through differential responses of mirrors made of different materials.
detection_principle: Sapphire and fused-silica mirrors have different compositions and accelerations under a B−L vector field; auxiliary length channels are searched for coherent narrowband oscillations.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2024 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Ultralight vector dark matter search using data from the KAGRA O3GK run

collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Data used
key_parameters.value: KAGRA auxiliary length channels during the joint KAGRA O3GK and GEO600 observing period

key_parameters.name: Design arm length
key_parameters.value: 3 km; the optical system includes cryogenic sapphire mirrors.

results.summary: Analysis of actual 2024 data found no credible signal and set coupling limits. Although weaker than some existing constraints, it demonstrates the feasibility of this low-mass search method.

science_scope: This analysis actually uses KAGRA's own data, unlike some other LVK publications whose authorship merely includes KAGRA. The instrument's gravitational-wave role does not change the direct-interaction nature of this ultralight-field search.
